Next month the 26th marks the first anniversary of the Tai Po Wang Fuk Court fire. The independent committee investigating the fire is expected to submit a report to the Chief Executive before the end of October. Recent reports indicate that the government has already activated the Department Head Accountability System to investigate the administrative responsibility for the blaze, and has redeployed political officials to assist. Chief Executive John Lee today (the 6th) did not respond to whether the mechanism has been activated, saying that the government has made a series of deployments and will push for reforms and accountability as soon as possible after the report is submitted. The Stanley luxury residence One Stanley has been exposed for having steel reinforcement bars that do not match the plans. John Lee said that the Buildings Department is investigating the case and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the investigation. With engineering projects being exposed for issues repeatedly, he said he values the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, which relates to the professionalism, quality, and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will strictly enforce the law.

The Wang Fuk Court fire is approaching its one-year mark. The independent committee is expected to submit a report before the end of October. (File photo)

Earlier media reports indicated that two political officials — former Deputy Secretary for Security Mok Kwan-yu and Commissioner for Sports Choi Kin-pan — would provide support to an investigation小组 under the Public Service Commission, specifically handling preliminary work on administrative accountability.

Chief Executive John Lee attended a press session before the Executive Council meeting today and was asked whether the matter is true. Does the activation of the Department Head Accountability System to investigate responsibility mean that even if there is a report, any accountability involving officials will not have immediate results, and how long will the public have to wait?

John Lee said that he made it clear from the start that after the independent committee submits its report, he would actively study and follow up on the recommendations, implement reforms, and announce the details. He did not directly respond to whether political officials have been redeployed to prepare for preliminary investigative work, saying only that "the government has made a series of deployments during this period," emphasising that after the report is submitted, based on its content, "comprehensive reforms will be implemented as soon as possible in the short term, and accountability will be pursued," with detailed announcements to be made at that time.

John Lee said that after the independent committee submits its report, reforms and accountability will be pursued as soon as possible based on the report's content. (File photo)

John Lee also reiterated multiple times that improvement measures cannot wait. Therefore, when delivering the Policy Address in September, he announced seven priority improvement measures, including banning smoking at construction sites, strengthening regulation of fire service installations, strengthening sanctions and punishment for professionals and contractors, improving compliance operations of owners' corporations, studying the criminalisation of bid-rigging, providing tendering and evaluation services for the first time, establishing pre-qualification lists for consultants and contractors, and studying proposals to better assist the public in professional projects.

According to records, the Public Service Commission is an independent statutory advisory body that advises the Chief Executive on civil service appointments, promotions, and disciplinary matters. The Department Head Accountability System was proposed by Chief Executive John Lee in last year's Policy Address, establishing a two-tier investigation mechanism based on the severity of departmental issues. If the issue is less serious in nature and involves an isolated incident, the department head will conduct the first-tier investigation. If the department has serious problems, or involves extensive, recurring systemic issues, or may involve the role of the department head, an investigation小组 led by the Public Service Commission will conduct the second-tier investigation.

The luxury residence One Stanley has been exposed for having steel reinforcement bars in a unit that do not match the plans. John Lee said he would not comment on the case which is still under investigation, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the Buildings Department's investigation.

One Stanley 'short on rebar' – requested Development Bureau to monitor investigation

Recently, construction projects have been exposed for issues one after another, including the tilting of lift shafts in the new block of Queen Mary Hospital, concrete samples at a Tung Chung public housing estate not meeting the strength standard, and steel reinforcement in floor slabs at the One Stanley luxury residence not matching the plans. John Lee was asked whether there are problems with construction and even project supervision?

Responding to the One Stanley project issue, he said the Buildings Department is seriously investigating the case, "to ascertain whether there are problems with construction quality and supervision, and will handle it strictly in accordance with the law." As the investigation is still ongoing, he would not comment on the details of the case, and has requested the Development Bureau to monitor the case investigation. However, he emphasised that he values the construction quality of Hong Kong's building projects, "is concerned about whether professionals related to the project have fulfilled their supervisory duties diligently, and whether contractors have violated regulations in construction," and said that it concerns the professionalism, quality, and safety of Hong Kong's construction industry, and the government will inevitably enforce the law strictly.

He has also requested the Development Bureau to enhance regulatory requirements and penalties in terms of legislation for overall construction projects, to ensure the deterrent effect of the law, severely punish relevant violators, and safeguard the professionalism, quality, and safety of Hong Kong's construction projects. The Development Bureau will submit proposed amendments to the Buildings Ordinance this year to strengthen supervision and enhance the penalty system and sanctions, and the authorities will push forward the relevant work at full speed.

The difficulty of nurse graduates finding jobs has recently drawn attention. John Lee said that demand for nurses has long existed, and pointed out that the Hospital Authority currently has more than 3,000 nurse vacancies, which graduates can apply for. (File photo)

ExCo member Tommy Cheung criticises 'unions posing as people' – John Lee says demand has long existed

Discussions on the difficulty of nurses finding jobs have heated up recently. The source was a phone-in segment on a radio programme after the Policy Address, in which a Mr Kwok, who claimed to be a psychiatric nurse in a disciplinary force, said his application for deferred retirement was not approved, and that his nursing graduate daughter became unemployed upon graduation, questioning the Hospital Authority's importation of Mainland medical personnel. ExCo member Tommy Cheung subsequently questioned whether it was the union "possibly posing as people to make calls," and declared that he fully supports importing talent from outside.

Reporters asked about the difficulty of nurse graduates finding jobs, how to resolve the concentration of openings in experienced nurses, and how to respond to ExCo members' remarks being accused of intensifying social conflicts. John Lee said that in every industry, there are situations where graduates do not seek employment immediately after graduation for individual reasons, or where recruiting organisations select those most suited to their needs, "resulting in some individuals not being hired." He emphasised that societal demand for nurses has always existed, especially as Hong Kong's healthcare continues to develop and the population ages, "so recruitment numbers will ultimately inevitably reflect this existing demand." He also pointed out without naming anyone, "there are different discussions in society on this aspect, allowing everyone to discuss the issue more clearly."

John Lee also said that according to 2025/26 figures, there are approximately 4,000 potential nurse graduates, with about 2,500 actually applying to the Hospital Authority, meaning 1,500 are applying for positions outside the Hospital Authority. The Hospital Authority currently still has more than 3,000 nurse vacancies, "nurse graduates can apply, and there is a chance of being hired."

Secretary for Health Professor Lo Chung-mau earlier accepted interviews with several media outlets to clarify that the government's recruitment policy definitely places local talent first. John Lee also reiterated that based on the current number of nurses in the Hospital Authority, "99.8% are locally trained nurses in Hong Kong," clearly implementing the local talent priority employment policy. He also said that currently 40% of nurses work in the public healthcare system, with the remaining 60% in other healthcare positions, such as community nursing, elderly care, rehabilitation services, and private medical institutions. He emphasised that societal demand for nurses has long existed. The government will, based on healthcare service needs, exchange views with the industry and academia, and do a good job in planning for healthcare professional training and manpower development.
